Brief description of general topic of vignette

## Conceptual Overview

### Standard K-Nearest Neighbors
- Explain equal-vote KNN and how distant neighbors hurt accuracy near boundaries or at large $k$.

### Distance-Weighted Voting
- Introduce inverse-distance weighting ($w_i = 1/d_i$) and how closer neighbors get more voting power

### Feature Scaling & Distance Metrics
- Explain why numeric features must be normalized before computing Euclidean distance. (Some variables are 0-1 while others are not bounded)

## Code Demonstration: Spotify Genre Classification

### Data Description & Setup
- Load R packages and the 2,700-row balanced Spotify sample (9 audio predictors + metadata IDs)

### Exploratory Data Analysis
- Some plots looking at the characteristics of the data

### Preprocessing & Train/Test Split
- Do an 80/20 stratified split in R, set metadata columns to "ID" role, and apply step_normalize()

### Model Specification & Hyperparameter Tuning
- Tune neighbors ($k$) and weight_func ("rectangular" vs. "inv") using 5-fold cross-validation (We are comparing "rectangular" (uniform) vs. "inv" (inverse-distance) across multiple values of $k$.)

### Comparing Uniform vs. Distance-Weighted Accuracy
- Plot CV accuracy across $k$ for both weighting methods and highlight where one wins (ideally same graph)

### Final Model Evaluation
- Fit the winning model on the test set, report final accuracy/AUC, and plot a confusion matrix

## Conclusion & Limitations
- Summarize key takeaways, when to use weighted KNN, and practical limitations (prediction speed, irrelevant features)
